1. **Chart type**  
   - **Line chart** (time series), with the final segment highlighted in a different color and endpoint annotations.

2. **Layout techniques**  
   - **Single-panel chart**
   - No faceting or small multiples
   - No stacking
   - Uses **highlighting** via color for the most recent segment/endpoints
   - Uses **direct labels/annotations** for 2022 and 2023 values

3. **Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year | Temporal | Position on x-axis; text labels for highlighted points (2022, 2023) |
| Average game duration | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; connected line; direct value labels for highlighted points (“3:08”, “2:39”) |
| Highlight status (recent segment vs rest) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of line and points (orange vs gray) |

comments.raw_comment: From the graph, it is clear that baseball games have increased in time duration as the decades went by, but recently in the year of twenty-twenty two, game durations have drastically decreased. Due to this hefty length, the MLB made efforts to reduce meeting times, pitch delivery times, increase base sizes, and change other factors that can cause the game to be longer. It is wondered if desires to reduce game duration was caused by loss of viewers due to the hefty time consumption. Rumors have spread that fan bases throughout baseball have been decreasing, it can be assumed that people do not want to have their time consumed by a baseball game and would rather just watch fragments of the game rather than spend their money and day's time to watch. Sports are a great source of entertainment, and corporations are always looking for ways to attract more fans in order to make more money. Rule changes such as this can greatly affect sporting events and the viewer ratings, overall this may cause people in my community to want to watch baseball more often than not. A catchy headline to capture the graphs main idea would be “A New Age of Baseball.”

On a related note, I notice that for every decade the end of the decade's average game duration is greater than the start of the decade's. Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  “A New Meaning to 'Fastball'” by Sami of Saint Thomas Aquinas High School in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; “Fast Ball: How Has the New Rule Changes Affected the Pace of the Game” by Vivi of Eden Prairie High School in Minnesota; "New Rules, Shorter Games, MLB Makes a Change!" by Grace and "Does 2023 Mark The End of Long Baseball Games?" by Jayna, both from Perth Amboy High School in New Jersey; and, "From Slowball to Fastball: How Baseball Games are Speeding Up" by Adam, “Heating Up: MLB Throws a Curveball with New Fast-Paced Games” by Dillon and “Baseball: America’s Pastime is Catching up to Speed” by Edy, all three from of California Polytechnic San Luis Obispo.
 
This is the last graph of the school year.  Looking forward to your returning and a new crop of graphs in early September.
 
Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who loves the relaxed baseball pastime but is looking forward to the excitement of a faster game, and Christine Franklin, American Statistical Association Statistical K-12 Ambassador and University of Georgia Emerita statistics faculty from Athens, Georgia, who LOVES attending and scoring baseballs games regardless of the length of the game.

1. I note that game time for baseball rose the greatest between 1985 and 1995 in this graph. Between the 2000s and 2005, game duration gradually decreased before increasing dramatically after that year. It peaked about 2020, with games lasting significantly longer than three hours. After 2020, the game's time reduced steadily, eventually reaching almost 3 hours.

2.  I'm curious why this drop is so significant. I expected that a timed pitch clock would shorten the game, but I had no clue by how much. I believe pitchers are suddenly concerned with pitching within the allotted time frame, and they are throwing much earlier than they would usually, even though there is still plenty of time on the pitch clock. They may sense the pressure of a time constraint and pitch earlier than they would usually. But I'm not sure if this is true for most pitchers these days, or just a subset of them.

3. This relates to my community because I come from a city where baseball is a prominent sport. I wonder how enjoyers of baseball will react to the average increase of baseball games just to suddenly drop in the current year.

4. "How Will New Game-Shifting Rules Change the MLB Forever"

comments.raw_comment: This graph demonstrates the evolution of the average duration of Major League Baseball games.  This graph was created in response to the league creating new rules to speed up the game, including a pitch clock, a limit on pickoff throws by the pitcher, and eliminating the shift.  The main thing that stands out from the graph is the largest decline in time which happened between 2022 and 2023.  This is most likely a direct result of the new rules to shorten the game.  For a majority of the years displayed on the graph, the average duration is between 2 hours and 45 minus and 3 hours.  It is also clear that in the last 10 years the games have been much longer, mostly over 3 hours.  Another thing that stands out is in 1980s, the games were even shorter than they are now.  I wonder why this occurred.  Was there less strategy 40 years ago?  Was there a pitch clock that was eliminated?  Did they have shorter innings due to less hitting?  This graph is relevant to me and my community because like myself, very few baseball fans could stand the amount of time the pitcher would take to throw the ball.  This makes the game far more captivating and will potentially draw in more viewers.  I would entitle this graph: "Less Time is Better in Baseball."

comments.raw_comment:
1. I discovered that an MLB game in 2023 will last as long as one from the 1980s. There was a noticeable rising trend in the average duration between the two time periods up until 2023. This graph's greatest fall, which occurred between 2022 and 2023, suggests that those years saw the implementation of the strictest new laws. The average game time was reduced to 2 hours and 39 minutes, a decrease of around 30 minutes.
2. I wonder what prompted the MLB to implement these new rules. Could implementing these new regulations make the game more interesting for baseball fans? Could the reason as to why games took longer be due to the lack of technology to review invalid plays? Could this have caused baseball fans from before to lose interest in the sport?
3. This relates to me and my community because baseball is one of the most popular sports so when it develops, I'm curious how competitions at the middle and high school levels will change. Also, it is now known that technology has taken over the entire world and how this could affect how people watch. Younger generations in particular have spent our entire lives viewing brief video clips and parts and haven't really had the attention span to sit through a 3-hour movie, much less a sporting event. It could be argued that shorter sporting events prevent viewers from getting bored and turning away because of the rising rates of indifference and impatience.
4. A Curveball Into Time!

comments.raw_comment:
Evan Morgans, Strath Haven High School

What do you notice? 
- I notice that the reduction of the game is about 29 minutes, which is quite a large amount of time taken from a sports game, especially baseball. I understand this change is meant to engage more people to watch games and to make the games more competitive, along with the addition of the other rules, though these changes don't seem necessary. Fielders are no longer allowed to adjust to certain batters, which feels like a nitpick more than a crucial change to the game. Most of these changes feel like exactly that, a nitpick to gain more revenue. 
What do you wonder?
- I wonder if these changes actually helped generate more viewers for games and if the games this season are actually "more competitive". 
Impact on community
- There's not much impact, since watching baseball is purely entertainment. Though to the baseball community, it's quite a big impact with generally mixed reviews. For regular viewers, this is only a negative since they would have already had the time to take to watch MLB games. Though now it's shorter, and they're missing a lot more of what they love about the sport, almost 30 minutes worth of time. Though for casual watchers who'll watch once in a while with family, this is a welcome change. They usually don't care enough to spend 3 hours of time to watch, so now when they decide to watch they have almost 30 minutes saved out of their day.

- Length of baseball games over the years

comments.raw_comment:
What I notice in this graph is that you can observe a steady increase in the duration of the baseball games from 1980 to 2020, with multiple peaks between the 1990s and 2000s. The average duration time hits its peak during 2020 before severely declining in 2022. I can also notice between 1990 and 2010, the average game duration time mostly stayed between  2 hours and 45 minutes to 3 hours.

I wonder if the effects and aftermath of COVID had something to do with the decline in game duration time since severe protocols were probably put in place. I also wonder if the new generation of baseball players affected how the games play out during the seasons making them shorter or their play decisions. Could this also do with the advertisements being broadcasted on live TV or the attention span of the audience as baseball evolved over time?

This relates to my community because it has been known that technology has taken over the whole world. Specifically with the younger generations, we are grown up watching short clips of videos and segments and never really had the attention span to sit through a 3-hour movie, much less a sports game. It could be said that the growing rate of inattention and impatience has led to the sports games being shorter so the watcher doesn't have the opportunity to be bored and keep watching.

My headline would be, "Pack Up Your Peanuts, Baseball Games Are Declining In Watch Time"

I noticed that the average duration of MLB games in 2023 is similar to the average duration of MLB games in the 1980s. In between the two time periods, there was a fairly strong positive trend of the average duration getting larger, until 2023. The change from 2022 to 2023 is the steepest drop in this graph, so these new rules must've been the most extreme ones implemented throughout the time period. 

I wonder what caused the MLB to implement these new rules. I do feel like more than 3 hours is quite a long time for games, so implementing these rules could make the game more efficient for baseball players and baseball fans alike. 

I’m a baseball fan, so this trend is definitely something I was cognizant of and excited to see. The pace of games is much quicker, more enjoyable to watch, and has increased action on the field. It certainly seems like players have adjusted pretty quickly and the game has improved for the better. 

"Short Stop: How Baseball Game Lengths Have Changed Over Time."

Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  This is our last release of this school year.  
Today’s graph shows the average “speed” of major league baseball games since 1980 for the first three weeks of each season.  New rules were instituted this season that include a clock to require pitchers and hitter to “play ball” with shorter delays, no more shifting players into the infield to make outs and making it easier to steal bases.  Is baseball going to get faster and more entertaining?  Could it be as exciting as its sport competitors – football, basketball and hockey?  Will in person and broadcasted audiences increase in size?
From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online for the four questions.  We have added a suggestion to the “What do you notice?” question.  If your notice includes a claim, please back it up with evidence that supports your claim.  
By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the free link to the online article that included these graphs.  

You can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

This is the last graph of the school year.  “See” you in early September.

I noticed that there was a sharp decrease in game duration between the 2022 and 2023 seasons. I also noticed that before the rule change, game duration had increased by about 30 minutes since 1980. Because there are many more televised games in the modern day, which tend to take much longer than non-televised games, it is interesting to see that the rule change alone was able to reduce the game duration back to what it was in the 80s.

I wonder what else has affected the average game duration over the last 40 years. The graph shows other fairly sharp drops and peaks, so I wonder if there were any rule changes or changes in MLB broadcasting that caused those changes in average game duration. I also wonder how players feel about the change, because it likely disrupts their game rhythm and requires them to adapt to a faster pace of play.

This relates to me because I have been a fan of the MLB for a while and I found the games to be slow and at times boring compared to other sports like basketball and football. I hope this change will make baseball more enjoyable to watch with less downtime between pitches.

Pitch Clocks: Changing the World of Baseball
I notice that in the graph there has been a steady increase of MLB game times from 1980 to 2020. However, in 2022-2023 there is a dramatic decrease. At the height of game times it was at roughly 3 hour and 10 minutes a game and then in 2022 it dropped to 3 hours and 8 minutes and then to a solid 2 hours and 39 minutes in 2023. I wonder why it took the MLB to instill this rule into the games until 2020, if they saw the increase, why did they wait so long? This relates to my community because i’ve gone to various baseball games and MLB games where i’ve recently seen the pitch clock be implemented. Although it does make baseball games shorter, I don’t think i’m rather fond of the pitch clock. It makes the game feel more rushed and there is less control that the players have in the game. I noticed a drop in the average game duration between 2022-2023. I also noticed since 1980, the average game duration averages above three hours. Between the highest point between the mid-1990s and the mid-2010s, a slight dip occurs in the mid-2000s. There could have been some rule changes to reduce time in this time period too. 2022-2023 has the steepest drop, most likely due to the pitch time and the pitcher and catcher getting transmitters so there would be less time stalling. I think the ban on infield shifting and larger bases would increase time on the field.

I wonder why and how these changes, especially the pitch clock, are being enforced. Are there penalties for going over the pitch clock? How much time is given to the pitcher's team?

This relates to me because I played baseball when I was younger and I enjoy watching MLB baseball games. I feel that the pitch clock and transmitters reduce the amount of time spent standing on the field. Because playing baseball is a team sport and a lot of time is used to communicate with both teams and all members. When I went to watch baseball games, I remember they took too long and it felt more like waiting for people at bat. With these changes, games will be faster.

What do you notice? 

I notice that from 1980 to 2022, the average duration of the games gradually increases.  Even though there have been several decreasing trends throughout the years, the overall trend from 1980 to 2022 has been increasing. However, the average duration of the games has decreased exponentially during the 2023 season after several new rules have been enforced. The average duration of the game is three hours and eight minutes for 2022 but it is two hours and thirty-nine minutes for 2023. The average duration of the game for 2023 closely matches the average duration of the game for 1980. 

What do you wonder?

I am interested to know which specific new rule enforced this season has affected the average duration of the games the most. Is the new rule enforcing the pitch clock the main reason why the average duration of the game has decreased for 2023? 

How does this relate to you and your community?

I am a college student and I have several classmates that are currently following several baseball games. Since there are many teenagers and adults that are interested in baseball games, having baseball games that last too long may make them lose interest. One of the main reasons is that many teenagers and adults need to study or work and they could not speed too much time watching baseball games.

Previously, baseball game durations witnessed regular fluctuations, however there was still a gradual increase in the overall average game duration. However, the 2022-2023 school year experienced a steep decline in average game duration that was almost as low as that of 1980. In those 40 years, there was never a shift that drastic. 

I wonder how closely the rule changes and this decrease in average game duration are related. Were the rule changes purely due to observations by the MLB, or was the MLB experiencing a sharp decline in viewership due to the seemingly never-ending games? Even for those who are not baseball fans, one thing most people are aware of is that baseball games tend to last hours on end. My prediction is that over time, people’s attention spans have gotten too short to sit through entire games. 

Baseball is a very popular sport in America. There are many baseball fans in my own community. The decision may impact this select community positively, as they can watch their favorite teams play without dedicating hours on end to watching games. However, it could also impact them negatively, as there are some baseball fans that enjoy the entire experience and do not want games to feel rushed. My prediction is that ordinary people might become more inclined to start watching baseball, however those who are already baseball fans might not appreciate this new change as much. 

Pitch Perfect or Not? The Sharp Decline of Baseball Game Durations

I notice that there is a dramatic drop in the average game duration for MLB games from 2022 to 2023. Looking at the graph before 2023, the average game duration was on a rocky but steady increase, having grown from ~2hr 35 mins in 1980 to ~3hr 12mins in 2022. In 2023, the average game length was 2hr 39 mins, nearly back to the average time over 40 years before.

I wonder why the average time increased so much before 2023. The description noted that this dramatic decrease in time is most likely due to the new rules put into place, especially the implication of the pitch clock. There are several other rules added, such as a ban on the infield shift and bigger bases. I wonder how these other changes may have also affected the shortened time.

This does not directly affect me because I would not identify myself as a baseball fan nor do I play baseball, but I have many friends and family members who are and I am sure that these changes and the shorter average duration of a game will change the way they watch and enjoy baseball.

I noticed a steep drop this year in MLB game lengths from 3:08 in 2022 to 2:39 in 2023. Since MLB implemented a pitch clock to speed up games, this drop in time makes sense. It’s interesting to examine how this trend has fluctuated over the years with game time reaching a high water mark in the early 2010s. Back in the 1980s, however, games were approximately 2.5 hours long - roughly the same as the times this year.

Given that the data was taken through the first three weeks of the season, I wonder if this plot would change if data from entire seasons were used. It’s possible that weather and seasonality might alter these numbers or if players got more used to the new rules changes. 

I’m a baseball fan, so this trend is definitely something I was cognizant of and excited to see. The pace of games are much quicker, more enjoyable to watch, and have increased action on the field. It certainly seems like players have adjusted pretty quickly and the game has improved for the better. 

A potential name for this graph might be “Pace of Play.”

I also wonder if game durations are related to the overall evolution of baseball players since the 1980s, since sportsmen and women have generally improved over time with new technologies, strategies, and training regimens. 1. I noticed that for the year 2023, the duration time hit its ultimate steepest and most drastic decrease. The difference is 29 minutes of reduction. I also noticed that around the year 2021, the average time duration had also hit its peak. The average time has consistently been changing since 1980 and has not been consistent for any year.
2. I wonder if the new rules were not implemented, would in future years the average time duration surpasses the 3 hr 15 min mark? I wonder if the baseball fans had anything to do with the change since they might have felt that a 3 hour game is a very long time. I also wonder what caused the 3 hour peak in the year 1995 since the averages of the other years were way lower. 
3. This relates to me and my community because my family loves to watch baseball but at home. The games are too long and most of us don't like being in one place for multiple hours. At home, watching the games on tv, we can do other things while the game is on but no one really sits and watches for the entire game time. If the average game time keeps reducing, we would probably go watch a game in person since it won't be as long.
4. Hit The Winning Home Run Before The Time Strikes You Out

comments.raw_comment:
The first thing I noticed, probably like most people, is the major decrease in the amount of time an average baseball game lasts from 2022 to 2023. The average game duration is almost the lowest it has ever been. This change is a direct effect of the new pitch clock that was implemented into the game, a rule that I personally think was great for the game. 

One thing I wonder is will we continue to see the same pitch clock moving forward, a new modified pitch clock, or will they get rid of it all together? I hope that they continue to grow of the current pitch clock and make it better.

This relates to me and my community because I am an athlete who grew up playing baseball along with other sports. My dad is a huge Red Sox's fan so I am as well. Although I don't really watch the MLB, I have kept up with the season to see how the new pitch clocks plays out.

Count Down to Efficiency: How the Pitch Clock is Shortening Baseball Games
